headline: CBA's net interest margin increased 9 bps year-on-year to 2.08% (from 1.99% in FY24). Excluding a 7 bps benefit from reduced liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, underlying NIM improved only 2 bps. The increase was primarily driven by +9 bps from capital, replicating portfolio and hedge earnings (replicating portfolio +5 bps, capital hedges +4 bps), partially offset by −7 bps from funding costs (increased deposit price competition) and −1 bps from adverse basis risk (wider bank bill/OIS spread). Treasury and Markets contributed +1 bps. Asset pricing and portfolio mix were flat.

drivers.narrative: Reduction in lower yielding liquid assets drove a 5 bps increase and institutional pooled lending facilities drove a 2 bps increase in margin. These have a broadly neutral impact on net interest income.
The bank states asset pricing was flat year-on-year, with no quantified sub-components disclosed.

Decreased margin by 7 bps driven by increased deposit price competition. The Retail Banking Services segment separately reported lower deposit margins 'mainly due to competition, unfavourable mix as customers shift to higher yielding deposits and the impact of declining interest rates' (ev-14).

The bank states portfolio mix was flat for the full year. The RBS segment separately noted 'favourable portfolio mix primarily due to the benefit of strong growth in average deposits relative to assets' (ev-18), but this was offset elsewhere at Group level.

Margin decreased 1 bps reflecting an increase in the average spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The RBS segment confirmed 'higher basis risk arising from an increase in the spread' (ev-16).

Increased margin by 9 bps driven by the net impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 bps) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 4 bps). The Highlights page attributes the modest overall NIM increase 'primarily to higher earnings on capital and replicating portfolio hedges' (ev-12).
Increased margin by 1 bps. The Highlights page notes 'higher income from Treasury and Markets' as a driver of the NIM increase (ev-21).

notable_items: Excluding liquids and pooled facilities, underlying NIM improved only 2 bps (ev-4, ev-11)

RBS divisional NIM decreased 3 bps to 2.50%, reflecting lower deposit margins, lower home lending margins, and higher basis risk, partly offset by higher replicating portfolio earnings, favourable mix, and higher equity earnings (ev-13 through ev-19)
limitations: The KPI table on page 20 shows a different Group-level NIM measure (2.50% FY25 vs 2.53% FY24, −3 bps) labeled 'Presented on a cash basis' with divisional breakdowns; however, no walk chart exists for that measure. The primary walk chart (page 28) covers the continuing operations basis NIM (2.08%/1.99%). The two measures differ because the KPI table includes all divisions while the walk chart excludes discontinued operations.
A second document corroborating the exact same FY24→FY25 NIM walk was not available; the FY24 results presentation covers FY23→FY24 only.

evidence_records.quote: [walk chart] NIM Movement since June 2024: Jun 24 Full Year 199 -> Jun 25 Full Year 208
Net interest margin (%) 2.08 1.99 9bpts

The Bank's net interest margin increased 9 basis points on the prior year to 2.08%. Excluding a 7 basis point increase in margin from a reduction in lower yielding liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, which have a broadly neutral impact on net interest income, net interest margin increased 2 basis points.
Asset pricing: Flat.
Portfolio mix: Flat.

Basis risk: Basis risk arises from the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The Bank's margin decreased 1 basis point reflecting an increase in the average spread.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 9 basis points driven by the net impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 4 basis points).
Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 1 basis point.
Funding costs: Decreased margin by 7 basis points driven by increased deposit price competition.
Excluding the mix effect of lower liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, margins improved by 2bpts.
The modest increase was primarily due to higher earnings on capital and replicating portfolio hedges, partly offset by the impact of increased competition on deposit pricing.
Net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year, reflecting:
Lower deposit margins mainly due to competition, unfavourable mix as customers shift to higher yielding deposits and the impact of declining interest rates;
Lower home lending margins principally reflecting elevated competition; and
The impact of higher basis risk arising from an increase in the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate; partly offset by
Higher earnings on the replicating portfolio;
Favourable portfolio mix primarily due to the benefit of strong growth in average deposits relative to assets; and
Higher earnings on equity.
Net Interest Income (NII) increased 5%, primarily driven by a 9 basis point increase in Net Interest Margin (NIM)

The increase in NIM was primarily driven by higher earnings on capital and replicating portfolio hedges, and higher income from Treasury and Markets, partly offset by the impact on deposit margins from increased competition and unfavourable basis risk.
